CHALLENGE C0137 | The regex `\bC\d{4}\b` strictly matches the canonical CDSFL finding ID format (C0001-C9999). Broadening it to `[A-Za-z]\d{3,5}` is incorrect and will improperly capture non-finding strings as entity references.
CHALLENGE C0141 | The proposed fix is functionally identical to the original code (`for i in sorted(indices):`) and does not resolve the sort order issue. The correct fix is to explicitly sort the resulting event list by timestamp, as proposed in C0087.

REOPEN C0008 | The caching bug in `verify()` remains in the target code. If `verify()` is called without a verifier, `self._verified` is set to `True`. Subsequent calls with a verifier return the cached result, entirely bypassing signature checks.
REOPEN C0009 | The `verify_bundle()` length mismatch vulnerability remains in the target code. The `zip()` function silently truncates to the shortest list, allowing unverified records to pass if `inclusion_proofs` is deliberately shortened.
REOPEN C0129 | The stale root bug in `export_bundle()` remains in the target code. Bundles exported while unsealed records exist will deterministically fail verification, as inclusion proofs are built against all records but the bundle root uses only the last epoch.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()` iterates over `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)`. It calls `verify_inclusion_proof` which successfully checks the proof against the root, but the method NEVER checks if the `record` actually corresponds to the `proof` (`record["chain_hash"] == proof["chain_hash"]`). Additionally, `zip()` silently truncates mismatched list lengths.
FOLLOW: An attacker can trivially bypass bundle verification by including completely forged or altered records, as long as they pair them with ANY valid inclusion proof from the chain. Furthermore, they can truncate the `inclusion_proofs` array to silently skip verification for trailing fake records. This completely breaks the trust model of exported evidence bundles.

FINDING_ID: F002

FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7
DESCRIPTION: FIND: In `EvidenceStore.export_bundle()`, when `epochs` is not empty, `merkle_root` is assigned the value of the last sealed epoch (`epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]`). However, the `inclusion_proofs` are built via `self._chain.build_inclusion_proof(i)`, which dynamically computes its target root against ALL appended records.
FOLLOW: If a bundle is exported containing any records while there are unsealed records at the head of the chain, the dynamic proof root will reflect all records and will not match the stale epoch root. `verify_bundle()` will deterministically fail for every record in the bundle, breaking end-to-end evidence export.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `EvidenceStore.verify()` caches its execution state in `self._verified` without considering whether a `verifier` was passed. 
FOLLOW: If a consumer first calls `verify()` to quickly check hashes, `self._verified` is cached as `True`. If the consumer later calls `verify(verifier=key)` to explicitly enforce authenticated attribution, the method returns the cached `True` immediately, skipping cryptographic signature verification entirely. Forged authenticated records will bypass detection.
